(a) Same skeleton as #2; only the ts_var window changes from 30 to 20, and the added cs_median(ts_var(LogFloatCap,50)) is a daily cross-sectional constant that cs_bucket_demean removes exactly. Its |rho| with #2 is 0.63, the highest in the library. It also has #2's (b)/trap-2 problems.

(b)/trap 1. Open is a positive back-adjusted price, so day_zero_ratio(Open) ties at 0 for nearly every stock. The ordinal _pct_rank inside cs_last_low05 then turns that tie block into a static ramp in column order. The only stock-specific content left is the bottom 5% of LogTotalCap, which direction -1 moves into the long book: a size step at the tail (trap 2). Its |rho| is at most 0.08 against every control and every other head, which fits a static ramp.

Trap 2. abs_(top-masked intraday corr(Ret,Open) x LogTotalCap rank) is mainly a market-cap rank: |rho| is 0.55 with market cap, 0.39 with liquidity and 0.37 with the known family. cs_last_low05(LogTotalCap, LogTotalCap) followed by abs_ folds the smallest 5% up to about 0.95-1, a V-shaped kink that a rank-cubic residual cannot remove. Multiplying by an abs'd, top-masked correlation is a numeric game.

Trap 2. day_zero_ratio(Ret) is multiplied by its own rank after cs_last_low05 has pushed the bottom 5% of LogTotalCap down. Every value in that bottom 5% is <=0 and every other value is >=0. Direction -1 therefore puts the smallest 5% of stocks by total cap into the long book as a block, whatever the signal says. That block is about half of the long decile and is a size tail step the rank-cubic residual cannot remove. The other half is picked by the lowest zero-return share, which has |rho| 0.42 with liquidity and 0.38 with the known family.
